convoLines.text: "When's the last time you really laughed?"
"Stealing joy. I like that. We should steal more of it."
"Still on the last time you laughed."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Colleen always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"I keep turning over the last thing Colleen said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Nobody says Colleen's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
You show them Mayapple — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Okay. That's — I need a minute. A long minute."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Did you leave someone behind? ...Sorry. You don't have to answer that."
Just: "Yeah." A long quiet. "Me too."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on who you left behind."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"I've got fires to light — metaphorical ones. Mostly."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You told me about the stolen laugh — someone tripping over nothing. Have you stolen any more since?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that personal stuff."
You show them Groundnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"They're already drifting away. "Later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Can I tell you something? At night I count the stars and name them after people."
Vikram has an edge today — something curdled.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Listen to me — Still on their secret."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
You show them Mayapple — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask? It'll keep."
"Are you going to stay? With us. For real."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

"Ernesto and I never did finish talking about what's been happening — that was 11 days back. You weren't there for that one — Ernesto was. Want to hear where it left off? 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.'"
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"My part? I remember them. Someone has to do it properly."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Between us — Still on what's been happening."
"...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "I dreamed Ernesto was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Good question." "I'd follow you out past the treeline. Don't tell the others — they'd want to come too."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Can I tell you something? I've been sneaking out at night. I'm ashamed and I can't stop."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
"Here. I made an extra." Nina presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on their secret. Worth considering."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
You show them Mayapple — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind? Simple as that."
"...Hi. Sorry. I'm not good at the talking-to-strangers part."
"What if it's not aliens? What if it's us — future us — running a simulation to figure out where we went wrong? We're homework."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Hey — I found some Groundnut today. You were right, it was right where you said."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"This wound — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Could you take a look?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"No, yeah, of course. Forget I asked." They won't forget. They'll just stop asking.
"Still on that favor."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Okay. I'll manage on my own."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to trading knowledge."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"You said yes — you left someone behind. I never asked who. I won't. But I'm still here, asking nothing, if that helps."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"What are you getting at?" A glance away, then back. They're choosing their words now.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Esteban rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "They took me. The Echo — up there, on the screens, in front of everyone. I'm still turning it over."
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
